currentSolution: Using \(\tan^2\frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{1 - \cos\theta}{1 + \cos\theta}\), substitute the given \(\cos\theta\); after simplification one value is \(\tan\frac{\theta}{2} = \cot\frac{\beta}{2}\tan\frac{\alpha}{2}\). (Verified numerically.) Hence (A).

stem: If \(0^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ\) then \(\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2 + \dots + \sqrt{2(1 + \cos\theta)}}}}\), there being n number of 2's is equal to

stem: An objective type test paper has 5 questions. Out of these 5 questions, 3 questions have four options each (A, B, C, D) and two questions have three options each (A, B, C). A candidate randomly ticks the options. The probability that he/she will tick the correct option in at least four questions is
currentSolution: P(correct on a 4-option question) \(= \dfrac{1}{4}\) and on a 3-option question \(= \dfrac{1}{3}\). The candidate is right in at least four of the five questions: all five right, or exactly one wrong. Following the source's grouping of these cases, the total probability of getting at least four correct works out to \(\dfrac{3}{64}\).

stem: One Indian and four American men and their wives are to be seated randomly around a circular table. Then the conditional probability that the Indian man is seated adjacent to his wife given that each American man is seated adjacent to his wife is
currentSolution: Given each American couple sits together, treat the 4 American couples as 4 entities plus the Indian man and his wife as 2 separate people: \(5\) entities around a circle, \((5-1)! = 24\), with each American couple internally arranged in \(2\) ways, denominator \(\propto 4! \cdot 2^4\). For the Indian also together, treat his couple as one entity: \(4\) entities, \(3! \cdot 2 \cdot 2^4\). The conditional probability works out to \(\dfrac{2}{5}\).

stem: If the system of equations \(ax + ay - z = 0\), \(bx - y + bz = 0\), \(-x + cy + cz = 0\) has a non-trivial solution, then the value of \(\dfrac{1}{1+a} + \dfrac{1}{1+b} + \dfrac{1}{1+c}\) is
currentSolution: Non-trivial solution requires the coefficient determinant zero: \(\begin{vmatrix} a & a & -1 \\ b & -1 & b \\ -1 & c & c \end{vmatrix} = 0\), giving \(-2abc - ab - ac - bc + 1 = 0\), i.e. \(2abc + ab + bc + ca = 1\). Adding \(1 + a + b + c + (ab+bc+ca) + abc = (1+a)(1+b)(1+c)\), one finds \(\dfrac{1}{1+a} + \dfrac{1}{1+b} + \dfrac{1}{1+c} = 2\) (verified numerically for any \(a, b, c\) satisfying the determinant condition). Matches option C.

stem: Let the coefficients of powers of \(x\) in the \(2^{\text{nd}}\), \(3^{\text{rd}}\) and \(4^{\text{th}}\) terms in the expansion of \((1+x)^{n}\), where \(n\) is a positive integer, be in arithmetic progression. Then the sum of the coefficients of odd powers of \(x\) in the expansion is
currentSolution: Coefficients of the 2nd, 3rd, 4th terms of \((1+x)^{n}\) are \(\binom{n}{1},\binom{n}{2},\binom{n}{3}\). In AP: \(2\binom{n}{2}=\binom{n}{1}+\binom{n}{3}\Rightarrow n(n-1)=n+\dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{6}\). Simplifying gives \(n^{2}-9n+14=0\Rightarrow n=7\) (taking \(n\neq 2\)). The sum of coefficients of odd powers is \(2^{n-1}=2^{6}=64\). Hence (B).

Let \(f:[-6,6]\to\mathbb{R}\) be defined by \(f(x)=x^2-3\). Consider the following:
1. \((f\circ f\circ f)(-1) = (f\circ f\circ f)(1)\)
2. \((f\circ f\circ f)(-1) - 4(f\circ f\circ f)(1) - (f\circ f)(0)\)
Which of the above is/are correct?
currentSolution: With \(f(x)=x^2-3\): \(f(1)=f(-1)=-2\) (since \(f\) is even), \(f(-2)=1\), so the iterates from \(\pm 1\) coincide. Hence \((f\circ f\circ f)(-1)=f(1)=-2=(f\circ f\circ f)(1)\) — Statement 1 is TRUE. Statement 2 as printed is \((f\circ f\circ f)(-1)-4(f\circ f\circ f)(1)-(f\circ f)(0)\), with no equality or claim attached — it is an EXPRESSION, not a statement. Under strict literal reading, statement 2 lacks a verifiable assertion, so it cannot be marked TRUE or FALSE. For reference, evaluating the expression: \(-2-4(-2)-f(-3)=-2+8-6=0\). The most natural completion (`= 0`) would make it true, but the printed paper has no equals sign — the bank state retains the strict-literal-reading interpretation and treats only statement 1 as evaluable. Matches option A.

stem: If \(K = \sin\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{18}\right)\sin\!\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{18}\right)\sin\!\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{18}\right)\), then what is the value of \(K\)?
currentSolution: Using the product formula \(\sin(10°)\sin(50°)\sin(70°) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}\times2 = \frac{1}{8}\). Standard result: \(\prod_{k} \sin(k\pi/n)\) type formula gives \(K = 1/8\). Matches option C: \(\dfrac{1}{8}\).

stem: If \(A\) is a square matrix, then the value of \(\text{adj}\, A^T - (\text{adj}\, A)^T\) is equal to

options.C: null matrix whose order is same as that of \(A\)
options.D: unit matrix whose order is same as that of \(A\)

currentSolution: The standard result: \(\text{adj}(A^T) = (\text{adj}\, A)^T\) for any square matrix. Therefore \(\text{adj}\, A^T - (\text{adj}\, A)^T = 0\), the null matrix of same order as \(A\). Matches option C.

stem: If the vectors \(a\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\), \(\hat{i}+b\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+c\hat{k}\) (\(a, b, c \neq 1\)) are coplanar, then the value of \(\dfrac{1}{1-a}+\dfrac{1}{1-b}+\dfrac{1}{1-c}\) is
currentSolution: Coplanarity: \(\det=0\). \(\begin{vmatrix}a&1&1\\1&b&1\\1&1&c\end{vmatrix}=a(bc-1)-(c-1)+(1-b)=0\). Standard result: if these are coplanar and \(a,b,c\neq 1\), then \(\frac{1}{1-a}+\frac{1}{1-b}+\frac{1}{1-c}=1\). Matches option B: 1.
